## Data Info
Number of **formative** reviews per reviewer 
```{r}
db <- ifelse(interactive(), "local/narrate.db", "../local/narrate.db")

rubric_version <- 5
last_modified <- format(file.info(db)$mtime, "%B %-d, %Y")

conn <- dbGetConn(db)

review_info <- tbl(conn, "review_assignment") |>
  left_join(
    tbl(conn, "reviewer") |> select(reviewer_id = id, human, username),
    by = "reviewer_id"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    tbl(conn, "evaluation") |> select(evaluation_id = id, summary_flg),
    by = "evaluation_id"
  ) |>
  filter(
    ((human == 1 & rubric_id == rubric_version & statusCode == 2) |
      (human == 0 & rubric_id == rubric_version & statusCode == 5)) &
      summary_flg == 0
  ) |>
  collect()

reviews_by_user <- review_info |>
  group_by(reviewer_id, username) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
reviews_by_user |> kable()
HTML(glue(
  "Data last modified {last_modified} - rubric version {rubric_version}"
))
```

## AI – Human Concordance (n = subset of formative evaluations we all coded)
```{r}
# Evaluations reviewed by every reviewer (AI + all humans)
n_reviewers <- n_distinct(review_info$reviewer_id)
shared_evals <- review_info |>
  distinct(evaluation_id, reviewer_id) |>
  count(evaluation_id) |>
  filter(n == n_reviewers) |>
  pull(evaluation_id)

shared_reviews <- review_info |>
  filter(evaluation_id %in% shared_evals) |>
  select(
    review_id = id,
    evaluation_id,
    human,
    sentiment = sentiment_score_value
  )

# Quality score on a 0-100 scale (sum of weighted, normalized components)
scores <- shared_reviews |>
  left_join(
    review_scores(conn, shared_reviews$review_id) |> select(-reviewer_id),
    by = "review_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(quality = 100 * (coverage + avg_specificity + utility))

# Quartiles of evaluations based on their mean quality score across all raters
eval_quartiles <- scores |>
  group_by(evaluation_id) |>
  summarise(eval_mean = mean(quality), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(quartile = ntile(eval_mean, 4))
scores <- scores |> left_join(eval_quartiles, by = "evaluation_id")

# Means across reviews; SDs are within-evaluation (between raters), averaged
# across evaluations
summarise_scores <- function(df, var, label) {
  df <- df |> mutate(value = {{ var }})
  per_eval <- df |>
    group_by(evaluation_id) |>
    summarise(
      sd_all = sd(value),
      sd_human = sd(value[human == 1]),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  tibble(
    Measure = label,
    mean_all = mean(df$value),
    mean_ai = mean(df$value[df$human == 0]),
    mean_human = mean(df$value[df$human == 1]),
    sd_all = mean(per_eval$sd_all),
    sd_human = mean(per_eval$sd_human)
  )
}

quartile_labels <- c("1st", "2nd", "3rd", "4th")
table1 <- bind_rows(
  summarise_scores(scores, quality, "Quality Score"),
  lapply(1:4, function(q) {
    summarise_scores(
      scores |> filter(quartile == q),
      quality,
      glue("&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;{quartile_labels[q]} Quartile")
    )
  }),
  summarise_scores(scores, sentiment, "Sentiment Score")
)

table1 |>
  kable(
    digits = 1,
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "",
      "Mean Score for All Raters",
      "Mean Score for AI Rater",
      "Mean Score for Human Raters",
      "Standard Deviation for All Raters",
      "Standard Deviation for Human Raters"
    )
  )
HTML(glue(
  "n = {length(shared_evals)} evaluations, {n_reviewers} reviewers ",
  "({n_distinct(review_info$reviewer_id[review_info$human == 1])} human)"
))
```

# AI – Human competency detection

For each competency, how often it was detected in the shared evaluations, and by
whom. Percentages are out of all shared evaluations ("H" = number of humans
that detected the competency in an evaluation).

**Summary**: each cell is *% of evaluations – mean specificity ± SD*.
Specificity is taken from the raters noted below, in the evaluations that
match the column.

- **Any**: at least one rater (AI or human) detected it. Specificity: all
  raters who detected it.
- **All**: the AI and every human detected it. Specificity: all raters.
- **AI**: the AI detected it, regardless of humans. Specificity: AI.
- **Human**: 2+ humans detected it, regardless of the AI. Specificity: humans
  who detected it.
- **AI + Human**: the AI and at least one human detected it. Specificity: all
  raters who detected it.
- **AI only**: the AI detected it, no human did. Specificity: AI.
- **Human only**: every human detected it, the AI did not. Specificity: humans.

```{r}
n_humans <- n_distinct(review_info$reviewer_id[review_info$human == 1])
n_evals <- length(shared_evals)

# All competencies on the rubric, so undetected ones still show up (0%)
rubric_comps <- tbl(conn, "rubric_competency") |>
  filter(rubric_id == rubric_version) |>
  left_join(
    tbl(conn, "competency") |> select(competency_id = id, name),
    by = "competency_id"
  ) |>
  select(competency_id, order, name) |>
  collect() |>
  arrange(order)

# One row per detected competency in a shared review
detections <- tbl(conn, "competency_score") |>
  filter(
    review_assignment_id %in% local(shared_reviews$review_id),
    !is.na(specificity)
  ) |>
  select(review_id = review_assignment_id, competency_id, specificity) |>
  collect() |>
  left_join(
    shared_reviews |> select(review_id, evaluation_id, human),
    by = "review_id"
  )

# Detection pattern per evaluation and competency: did the AI detect it and
# how many humans did
patterns <- detections |>
  group_by(evaluation_id, competency_id) |>
  summarise(
    ai = any(human == 0),
    n_human = n_distinct(review_id[human == 1]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# One cell per competency for evaluations matching `pattern`. Specificity is
# taken from `raters` ("all", "ai" or "human") in those evaluations
detection_cells <- function(pattern, raters = "all", with_spec = TRUE) {
  matched <- patterns |> filter(!!pattern)
  sapply(rubric_comps$competency_id, function(comp) {
    comp_matched <- matched |> filter(competency_id == comp)
    perc <- sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * nrow(comp_matched) / n_evals)
    spec <- detections |>
      semi_join(comp_matched, by = c("evaluation_id", "competency_id")) |>
      filter(raters == "all" | human == (raters == "human")) |>
      pull(specificity)
    if (!with_spec || length(spec) == 0) {
      return(perc)
    }
    spec_sd <- if (length(spec) > 1) sprintf(" ± %.1f", sd(spec)) else ""
    glue("{perc} – {sprintf('%.1f', mean(spec))}{spec_sd}")
  })
}

summary_cols <- list(
  "Any" = list(rlang::expr(TRUE), "all"),
  "All" = list(rlang::expr(ai & n_human == n_humans), "all"),
  "AI" = list(rlang::expr(ai), "ai"),
  "Human" = list(rlang::expr(n_human >= 2), "human"),
  "AI + Human" = list(rlang::expr(ai & n_human >= 1), "all"),
  "AI only" = list(rlang::expr(ai & n_human == 0), "ai"),
  "Human only" = list(rlang::expr(!ai & n_human == n_humans), "human")
)

tibble(
  Competency = rubric_comps$name,
  !!!lapply(summary_cols, function(col) detection_cells(col[[1]], col[[2]]))
) |>
  kable()
HTML(glue(
  "n = {n_evals} formative evaluations reviewed by the AI and {n_humans} humans"
))
```

**Breakdown**: every detection pattern, split by whether the AI detected the
competency and by how many humans did. Columns don't overlap, so each row sums
to the *Any* column above.

- **AI + *k*H**: the AI and exactly *k* humans detected it.
- **AI only**: the AI detected it, no human did.
- ***k*H only**: exactly *k* humans detected it, the AI did not.

```{r}
breakdown_cols <- c(
  setNames(
    lapply(n_humans:0, function(k) rlang::expr(ai & n_human == !!k)),
    c(glue("AI + {n_humans:1}H"), "AI only")
  ),
  setNames(
    lapply(n_humans:1, function(k) rlang::expr(!ai & n_human == !!k)),
    glue("{n_humans:1}H only")
  )
)

tibble(
  Competency = rubric_comps$name,
  !!!lapply(breakdown_cols, detection_cells, with_spec = FALSE)
) |>
  kable()
HTML(glue(
  "n = {n_evals} formative evaluations reviewed by the AI and {n_humans} humans"
))
```


# Does the AI agree with humans as well as humans agree with each other?
Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC)

Is the AI at least as good a rater as the average human? Non-inferiority test
on Δ = (mean AI–human pairwise ICC) − (mean human–human pairwise ICC). Each
pairwise ICC is ICC(2,1): two-way random effects, absolute agreement, single
rater, computed on the evaluations all raters coded. Absolute agreement means a
systematic shift in the AI's scores lowers its ICC, so bias is penalised too.

- **Margin (pre-specified): 0.10.** On the Koo & Li (2016) reliability bands
  (< 0.50 poor, 0.50–0.75 moderate, 0.75–0.90 good, > 0.90 excellent) each band
  is 0.15–0.25 wide, so a drop of less than 0.10 can't move the AI down a full
  band from where the humans sit.
- **CI:** 90% percentile bootstrap over evaluations. Both terms of Δ are
  recomputed on the same resample, so the CI accounts for their correlation.
  A two-sided 90% CI matches a one-sided test at α = 0.05.
- **Primary test, non-inferiority** (H₀: Δ ≤ −0.10): the AI is non-inferior if
  the lower bound of the CI is above −0.10. If the upper bound is below −0.10,
  the AI is inferior; anything else is inconclusive.
- **Secondary test, superiority** (H₀: Δ ≤ 0): only tested if non-inferiority
  holds. The AI is superior if the lower bound of the CI is above 0, i.e. it
  agrees with humans better than humans agree with each other. Testing in this
  fixed order keeps the overall α at 0.05 without a multiplicity correction.
- **p-values:** one-sided bootstrap p-values, the share of resamples at or
  below the null boundary, computed as (k + 1) / (B + 1) so they are never 0.
  They agree with the CI: p < 0.05 exactly when the lower bound clears the
  boundary. Note that the non-inferiority p-value tests against −0.10, not 0;
  a small value means the AI is *not* meaningfully worse.

```{r}
#| label: icc-bootstrap
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr file.mtime(db)
ni_margin <- 0.10
n_boot <- 2000
set.seed(20261027)

ai_ids <- unique(review_info$reviewer_id[review_info$human == 0])
human_ids <- unique(review_info$reviewer_id[review_info$human == 1])
rater_pairs <- combn(c(ai_ids, human_ids), 2, simplify = FALSE)
pair_type <- sapply(rater_pairs, function(p) {
  ifelse(any(p %in% ai_ids), "ai_human", "human_human")
})
pair_label <- sapply(rater_pairs, function(p) {
  paste(
    reviews_by_user$username[match(p, reviews_by_user$reviewer_id)],
    collapse = " – "
  )
})

# One row per evaluation, one column per rater
rater_matrix <- function(var) {
  scores |>
    left_join(
      review_info |> select(review_id = id, reviewer_id),
      by = "review_id"
    ) |>
    select(evaluation_id, reviewer_id, value = {{ var }}) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = reviewer_id, values_from = value) |>
    select(-evaluation_id) |>
    as.matrix()
}

pairwise_icc <- function(m) {
  sapply(rater_pairs, function(p) {
    irr::icc(
      m[, as.character(p)],
      model = "twoway",
      type = "agreement",
      unit = "single"
    )$value
  })
}

icc_delta <- function(iccs) {
  mean(iccs[pair_type == "ai_human"]) - mean(iccs[pair_type == "human_human"])
}

# One-sided bootstrap p-value for H0: delta <= boundary
boot_p <- function(boot_delta, boundary) {
  (sum(boot_delta <= boundary) + 1) / (length(boot_delta) + 1)
}

format_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))

# Non-inferiority then superiority from bootstrap draws of delta (negative =
# AI worse). Returns raw stats plus formatted table columns.
ni_test <- function(boot_delta, margin, digits = 3) {
  boot_delta <- boot_delta[!is.na(boot_delta)]
  delta_ci <- unname(quantile(boot_delta, c(0.05, 0.95)))
  p_ni <- boot_p(boot_delta, -margin)
  p_sup <- boot_p(boot_delta, 0)
  ci_fmt <- glue("[%.{digits}f, %.{digits}f]")
  list(
    stats = list(delta_ci = delta_ci, p_ni = p_ni, p_sup = p_sup),
    columns = tibble(
      ci = sprintf(ci_fmt, delta_ci[1], delta_ci[2]),
      p_ni = format_p(p_ni),
      # Superiority is only tested once non-inferiority holds
      p_sup = ifelse(p_ni < 0.05, format_p(p_sup), "–"),
      conclusion = case_when(
        p_ni < 0.05 & p_sup < 0.05 ~ "Non-inferior and superior",
        p_ni < 0.05 ~ "Non-inferior",
        delta_ci[2] < -margin ~ "Inferior",
        TRUE ~ "Inconclusive"
      )
    )
  )
}

non_inferiority <- function(var, label) {
  m <- rater_matrix({{ var }})
  iccs <- pairwise_icc(m)
  boot_delta <- replicate(n_boot, {
    icc_delta(pairwise_icc(m[sample(nrow(m), replace = TRUE), ]))
  })
  test <- ni_test(boot_delta, ni_margin)
  list(
    summary = tibble(
      Measure = label,
      icc_ai_human = mean(iccs[pair_type == "ai_human"]),
      icc_human_human = mean(iccs[pair_type == "human_human"]),
      delta = icc_delta(iccs)
    ) |>
      bind_cols(test$columns),
    pairs = tibble(Measure = label, Pair = pair_label, ICC = iccs),
    # Unformatted values for the results text
    stats = test$stats
  )
}

ni_results <- list(
  non_inferiority(quality, "Quality Score"),
  non_inferiority(sentiment, "Sentiment Score")
)

bind_rows(lapply(ni_results, `[[`, "summary")) |>
  kable(
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "",
      "Mean AI–Human ICC",
      "Mean Human–Human ICC",
      "Δ (AI–Human − Human–Human)",
      "90% Bootstrap CI for Δ",
      glue("p Non-inferiority (H₀: Δ ≤ −{ni_margin})"),
      "p Superiority (H₀: Δ ≤ 0)",
      glue("Conclusion (margin = {ni_margin})")
    )
  )
HTML(glue(
  "n = {length(shared_evals)} evaluations, {n_boot} bootstrap resamples; ",
  "{sum(pair_type == 'ai_human')} AI–human and ",
  "{sum(pair_type == 'human_human')} human–human rater pairs"
))
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
# Results sentence for the quality score, ready to copy into the paper
p_text <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p))
}

quality_ni <- ni_results[[1]]
q_sum <- quality_ni$summary
q_stats <- quality_ni$stats

ni_sentence <- if (q_stats$p_ni < 0.05) {
  glue(
    "The AI was non-inferior at the pre-specified margin of {ni_margin} ",
    "({p_text(q_stats$p_ni)})"
  )
} else {
  glue(
    "Non-inferiority at the pre-specified margin of {ni_margin} was not ",
    "shown ({p_text(q_stats$p_ni)})"
  )
}
sup_sentence <- if (q_stats$p_ni >= 0.05) {
  ""
} else if (q_stats$p_sup < 0.05) {
  glue(", and superior to human–human agreement ({p_text(q_stats$p_sup)}).")
} else {
  glue(", but not shown to be superior ({p_text(q_stats$p_sup)}).")
}
if (sup_sentence == "") {
  ni_sentence <- paste0(ni_sentence, ".")
}

cat(glue(
  "\n\n> Agreement on Quality between the AI and human raters was comparable to ",
  "agreement among humans (mean ICC {sprintf('%.2f', q_sum$icc_ai_human)} vs ",
  "{sprintf('%.2f', q_sum$icc_human_human)}; ",
  "Δ = {sprintf('%.3f', q_sum$delta)}, 90% CI ",
  "{sprintf('%.3f', q_stats$delta_ci[1])} to ",
  "{sprintf('%.3f', q_stats$delta_ci[2])}). ",
  "{ni_sentence}{sup_sentence}\n\n"
))
```

Pairwise ICCs

```{r}
bind_rows(lapply(ni_results, `[[`, "pairs")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Measure, values_from = ICC) |>
  kable(digits = 3)
```

# Does the AI agree with humans across quality levels?
Disagreement in score points (Quality Score only)

ICC can't be compared within subgroups: restricting to similar-quality texts
shrinks the between-text variance, so every ICC drops regardless of how well
raters agree. Instead, per evaluation we measure disagreement on the 0–100
quality scale:

- **AI disagreement** = mean |AI − human| over the human raters.
- **Human disagreement** = mean |human − human| over the human–human pairs.
- **Δ (points)** = human disagreement − AI disagreement, so like the ICC Δ,
  negative means the AI agrees less well than humans do with each other.

Quality level is the **human-only** mean quality score of the evaluation, so
the AI's own score doesn't decide which group a text falls in.

- **Margin: a small effect, 0.2 × between-evaluation SD.** The SD of the
  human-mean quality score across evaluations is how much reviews genuinely
  differ in quality, i.e. what the score is meant to detect. Following Cohen's
  convention for a small effect (d = 0.2), the AI's disagreement may exceed
  human disagreement by no more than 0.2 of that SD, on average. The margin was
  set after the ICC analysis, so the table also gives the **smallest passing
  margin** (minus the lower CI bound): the AI is non-inferior for any margin
  above it, so readers can apply their own.
- **Tests:** the same non-inferiority then superiority procedure, 90% bootstrap
  CIs and one-sided p-values as for the ICC, overall and within tertiles of
  quality.
- **Trend:** the slope of Δ on quality level (per 10 points). A slope near 0
  means the AI's relative performance doesn't change with quality.
- **Caveats:** near the ends of the scale both disagreements are compressed
  (floor/ceiling), and quality level and human disagreement share the same
  human scores, which slightly biases the slope.

```{r}
#| label: disagreement-bootstrap
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr file.mtime(db)
#| dependson: icc-bootstrap
set.seed(20261027)

quality_m <- rater_matrix(quality)
ai_col <- as.character(ai_ids)
human_cols <- as.character(human_ids)
human_pairs <- combn(human_cols, 2, simplify = FALSE)

tertile_labels <- c("Low", "Middle", "High")
disagreement <- tibble(
  human_mean = rowMeans(quality_m[, human_cols]),
  d_ai = rowMeans(abs(quality_m[, ai_col] - quality_m[, human_cols])),
  d_hh = rowMeans(sapply(human_pairs, function(p) {
    abs(quality_m[, p[1]] - quality_m[, p[2]])
  }))
) |>
  mutate(
    delta_pts = d_hh - d_ai,
    tertile = ntile(human_mean, 3)
  )

# Margin = small effect (Cohen's d = 0.2) relative to how much evaluations
# differ in quality; fixed on the full data, not re-estimated per resample
margin_effect_size <- 0.2
quality_sd <- sd(disagreement$human_mean)
pts_margin <- margin_effect_size * quality_sd

# Each resample: overall delta, slope per 10 points, and delta per tertile
pts_boot <- replicate(n_boot, {
  b <- disagreement[sample(nrow(disagreement), replace = TRUE), ]
  c(
    overall = mean(b$delta_pts),
    slope = 10 * coef(lm(delta_pts ~ human_mean, data = b))[["human_mean"]],
    sapply(1:3, function(t) mean(b$delta_pts[b$tertile == t]))
  )
})

points_row <- function(df, boot_delta, label) {
  test <- ni_test(boot_delta, pts_margin, digits = 1)
  list(
    row = tibble(
      Group = label,
      n = nrow(df),
      quality_range = sprintf(
        "%.0f–%.0f",
        min(df$human_mean),
        max(df$human_mean)
      ),
      d_ai = mean(df$d_ai),
      d_hh = mean(df$d_hh),
      delta = mean(df$delta_pts)
    ) |>
      bind_cols(test$columns) |>
      # Non-inferior for any margin above minus the lower CI bound
      mutate(min_margin = max(0, -test$stats$delta_ci[1]), .after = ci),
    # Unformatted values for the results text
    stats = test$stats
  )
}

# Overall first, then one entry per tertile
pts_results <- c(
  list(points_row(disagreement, pts_boot["overall", ], "All evaluations")),
  lapply(1:3, function(t) {
    points_row(
      disagreement |> filter(tertile == t),
      pts_boot[2 + t, ],
      glue("&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;{tertile_labels[t]} quality")
    )
  })
)

bind_rows(lapply(pts_results, `[[`, "row")) |>
  kable(
    digits = 1,
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "",
      "n",
      "Quality Range (human mean)",
      "AI Disagreement (points)",
      "Human Disagreement (points)",
      "Δ (Human − AI Disagreement)",
      "90% Bootstrap CI for Δ",
      "Smallest Passing Margin (points)",
      glue("p Non-inferiority (H₀: Δ ≤ −{sprintf('%.1f', pts_margin)})"),
      "p Superiority (H₀: Δ ≤ 0)",
      glue("Conclusion (margin = {sprintf('%.1f', pts_margin)} points)")
    )
  )

slope_est <- 10 *
  coef(lm(delta_pts ~ human_mean, data = disagreement))[[
    "human_mean"
  ]]
slope_ci <- quantile(pts_boot["slope", ], c(0.05, 0.95))
HTML(glue(
  "Margin = {margin_effect_size} × {sprintf('%.1f', quality_sd)} ",
  "(SD of human-mean quality across evaluations) = ",
  "{sprintf('%.1f', pts_margin)} points; ",
  "{n_boot} bootstrap resamples. ",
  "Slope of Δ on quality level: {sprintf('%.2f', slope_est)} points per 10 ",
  "quality points (90% CI {sprintf('%.2f', slope_ci[1])} to ",
  "{sprintf('%.2f', slope_ci[2])})"
))
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
# Results sentence for disagreement across quality levels, ready to copy into
# the paper (p_text() is defined with the ICC results sentence)
pts_overall <- pts_results[[1]]
pts_tertiles <- pts_results[-1]
tertile_p_ni <- sapply(pts_tertiles, function(r) r$stats$p_ni)
tertile_ni <- tertile_p_ni < 0.05
tertile_p <- glue("{tolower(tertile_labels)}, {p_text(tertile_p_ni)}")

overall_sentence <- glue(
  "Using a non-inferiority margin of {sprintf('%.1f', pts_margin)} points ",
  "({margin_effect_size} × the between-evaluation SD of ",
  "{sprintf('%.1f', quality_sd)}), the AI was ",
  "{ifelse(pts_overall$stats$p_ni < 0.05, '', 'not shown to be ')}",
  "non-inferior overall ({p_text(pts_overall$stats$p_ni)})"
)
tertile_sentence <- if (all(tertile_ni)) {
  glue(
    " and within each tertile of quality ",
    "({paste(tertile_p, collapse = '; ')})."
  )
} else {
  glue(
    ". Within tertiles of quality, non-inferiority was shown for ",
    "{if (any(tertile_ni)) paste(tertile_p[tertile_ni], collapse = '; ') else 'none'}",
    " but not for ",
    "{paste(tertile_p[!tertile_ni], collapse = '; ')}."
  )
}
slope_sentence <- if (slope_ci[1] < 0 && slope_ci[2] > 0) {
  "did not change with"
} else {
  "changed with"
}

cat(glue(
  "\n\n> Across quality levels, the AI's disagreement with human raters was ",
  "comparable to the disagreement among humans (mean absolute difference ",
  "{sprintf('%.1f', pts_overall$row$d_ai)} vs ",
  "{sprintf('%.1f', pts_overall$row$d_hh)} points on the 0–100 quality score; ",
  "Δ (human − AI disagreement) = {sprintf('%.1f', pts_overall$row$delta)}, ",
  "90% CI {sprintf('%.1f', pts_overall$stats$delta_ci[1])} to ",
  "{sprintf('%.1f', pts_overall$stats$delta_ci[2])}). ",
  "{overall_sentence}{tertile_sentence} ",
  "The difference {slope_sentence} quality level (slope ",
  "{sprintf('%.2f', slope_est)} points per 10 quality points, 90% CI ",
  "{sprintf('%.2f', slope_ci[1])} to {sprintf('%.2f', slope_ci[2])}).\n\n"
))
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Per-evaluation disagreement by quality level, with linear fits."

rater_colors <- c("AI vs human" = "#2a78d6", "Human vs human" = "#eb6834")

disagreement |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    c(d_ai, d_hh),
    names_to = "comparison",
    values_to = "points"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    comparison = ifelse(comparison == "d_ai", "AI vs human", "Human vs human")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(human_mean, points, color = comparison, shape = comparison)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = rater_colors) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
  labs(
    x = "Quality score (mean of human raters)",
    y = "Mean absolute disagreement (points)",
    color = NULL,
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Δ (human − AI disagreement) by quality level, with linear fit and 90% confidence band. The dashed line is the non-inferiority margin (0.2 × between-evaluation SD); it applies to the average, i.e. the fitted line and band, not to individual evaluations."
disagreement |>
  ggplot(aes(human_mean, delta_pts)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -pts_margin, color = "grey40", linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = max(disagreement$human_mean),
    y = -pts_margin,
    label = glue("Margin (−{sprintf('%.1f', pts_margin)})"),
    hjust = 1,
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 3.5,
    color = "grey30"
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.7, color = rater_colors[["AI vs human"]]) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    level = 0.90,
    color = rater_colors[["AI vs human"]],
    fill = rater_colors[["AI vs human"]],
    alpha = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Quality score (mean of human raters)",
    y = "Δ (human − AI disagreement, points)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
